observations.claim: The reviewed bytes invoke the v32 pre-council consistency audit but contain no audit finding identifier (CS-01..CS-09, CH-01..CH-03, CA-01, BA-01..BA-04) and no per-finding closure mapping, so the required demonstration that each pinned audit finding is closed in v33 cannot be checked from the reviewed artifact.
observations.evidence_excerpt: Corrected after the v32 pre-council consistency audit; requires deterministic audit checks
observations.impact: A mandatory closure property is asserted only implicitly; any 'closed' conclusion would rest on an artifact not present in this lane.
observations.recommended_action: Require a per-finding closure table mapping every pinned audit finding ID to an exact v33 section/line locator and, where applicable, its validator or fixture, before a closure claim is relied on.

observations.claim: The design's root-cause evidence basis is an external snapshot path plus hash, while this lane's pinned bytes contain only the sanitized design; the failure-model bytes and the v32 audit are therefore unavailable for re-derivation in this review.
observations.evidence_excerpt: The evidence-bound failure model used for v32 is the immutable snapshot
observations.impact: Root-cause and counterfactual claims in Section 2 cannot be independently recomputed from the reviewed bytes, so their evidentiary weight is a function of an unpinned read.
observations.recommended_action: Supply the referenced snapshot/audit bytes with this lane, or record the context reduction explicitly as a degradation and cap any evidence-dependent conclusion accordingly.

observations.claim: The charge-preimage candidate persisted before the ledger write commits an allocated_attempt_id inside attempt_invariants, while Section 5.1 states that none of the six pre-charge control effects may allocate an attempt.
observations.evidence_excerpt: attempt_invariants` as the closed JCS object `{source_attempt_ids_sha256,source_attempt_count,source_attempts_charged,allocated_attempt_id
observations.impact: The boundary between persisting a candidate attempt ID and allocating an attempt is not pinned; the pre-charge allowlist and the charge-intent construction can be read as mutually inconsistent.
observations.recommended_action: State explicitly that a pre-charge intent may carry only a candidate attempt ID that becomes allocated solely by the version-guarded ledger write, and align Section 5.1 with Section 5.2 steps 4-6.

observations.claim: The normative composed transition table does not name several states that Sections 9.1 and 14 define (for example INTENT_INDEX_OPEN_PENDING, UNCHARGED_COMPLETION_CORRUPT_BLOCKED, COMPLETION_CORRUPT_BLOCKED, ADMIN_LEDGER_APPEND_UNKNOWN_BLOCKED), so state/edge completeness is owned by three sections rather than one enumerable table.
observations.evidence_excerpt: This table plus Sections 5.1–9.1 is normative; an omitted state/edge is forbidden.
observations.impact: A reviewer or validator cannot decide 'no missing state edge' from the table alone; reconciliation across Sections 5.0.1, 9.1 and 14 is required and may differ on entry/exit conditions.
observations.recommended_action: Publish one canonical machine-checkable state/edge enumeration and have the composed table, failure matrix and fixture manifest reference it by ID.

observations.claim: The logical intent ID preimage uses previous_head_hash and previous_head_sequence, terms that appear nowhere else in the design, while Sections 9.1 and 5.2 use previous_completion_hash/previous_completion_sequence and 'closed-chain head'.
observations.impact: An implementer cannot determine from the text which persisted value feeds the deterministic logical intent ID, which weakens the claimed byte-exact reproducibility of intent hashes and OPEN entries.
observations.recommended_action: Declare one canonical name for the chain-head pair, define it once in the hash-domain profile (Section 5.1.1), and replace the aliases.

observations.claim: Section 6.3 requires the AdmissionResourceReservation append (effect 5.1(f)) to be the first admission-cycle operation, but Section 5.1 also places the AIP/ASC start transition (effect 5.1(a)) on the FROZEN to PREPARING edge without stating whether that effect precedes the reservation or is metered by it.
observations.evidence_excerpt: Before any ordinary admission-cycle call/effect, effect 5.1(f) appends one immutable `AdmissionResourceReservation` as the first operation.
observations.impact: A pre-PREPARING AIP/ASC effect may be read as either unmetered relative to the administrative ceiling or double-charged, which bears on the no-hidden-cost and no-double-debit properties.
observations.recommended_action: State the exact total order of effects (a) through (f) and name the ledger allocation that prices the FROZEN-to-PREPARING AIP transition.

observations.claim: Section 16 requires a closed transition-capability manifest whose missing cells block drafting, but the reviewed bytes contain no such manifest or fixture inventory, so fixture completeness for every declared state and edge cannot be checked in this review.
observations.impact: The design's central completeness claim is deferred to an artifact produced after this review; absent it, the transition table and failure matrix cannot be shown to be fixture-backed.
observations.recommended_action: Require the manifest and its passing-fixture references as a reviewable artifact at the next gate, and treat its absence as verification-not-verifiable rather than a satisfied must-check.

observations.claim: The design explicitly limits its enforcement claim to procedural fail-closed governance and discloses both the delegated-writer bypass and the external-state TOCTOU residual rather than claiming non-bypassable enforcement.
observations.evidence_excerpt: Therefore this design claims **procedural fail-closed governance**, not hard runtime enforcement.
observations.impact: Readers and the HUMAN decision owner can distinguish a procedural coordinator gate from native prevention, which is the property Section 16 requires to be disclosed in the approval packet.
observations.recommended_action: Retain this wording unchanged and confirm the same disclosure is present verbatim in the WBS approval packet.

observations.claim: Authority over the attempt ceiling, reallocation and the contingency reserve is retained by the HUMAN decision owner, with council output explicitly excluded from setting the operative amount.
observations.evidence_excerpt: Only the HUMAN decision owner may select or change the operative amount; council output is advisory and cannot set it.
observations.impact: The advisory boundary is explicit, so no council or model output can be misread as a ceiling or contingency decision.
observations.recommended_action: Retain; verify that the later WBS approval record binds the exact selected revision/hash to the HUMAN ceiling decision.

observations.claim: Section 5's diagram routes a HUMAN-accepted ledger genesis to FROZEN and requires a separate exact HUMAN bootstrap authorization to enter BOOTSTRAP_MAINTENANCE, while Section 6.3 states that the genesis final acceptance itself authorizes BOOTSTRAP_MAINTENANCE.
observations.evidence_excerpt: makes sequence zero usable and authorizes `BOOTSTRAP_MAINTENANCE`
observations.impact: Whether genesis acceptance alone admits maintenance work, or must pass back through FROZEN first, is not pinned; a reader could treat one decision as sufficient where the diagram requires two.
observations.recommended_action: State the single authoritative edge from ADMIN_LEDGER_GENESIS into BOOTSTRAP_MAINTENANCE and reconcile the diagram, Section 6.3 and the transition table.

advisory_hypotheses.claim: If the existing dsh-wbs-execution/1 contract is validated strictly, representation (a) may have no proven slot for the mandated /charge_boundary_preflight_sha256 pointer, which would make the charge preimage unconstructible without inventing a field.
advisory_hypotheses.basis: Section 5.2 step 4 enumerates representation (a) as covering attempt allocation, cumulative charge, bundle hash, seal hash, boundary-receipt hash, lineage and attempt ID, while step 5 requires the candidate tree to contain exactly the selected execution-contract pointer /charge_boundary_preflight_sha256.
missing_project_sot: The exact pinned dsh-wbs-execution/1 schema bytes, validator implementation and strict-validator fixtures.
advisory_hypotheses.suggested_validation: Load the pinned schema and validator, build the candidate tree with the preflight pointer present, and run the strict validator; if it rejects the field, record P15 NOT_READY or restrict the decision to representation (b).

advisory_hypotheses.claim: The version-guarded execution.json write may rely on a native guarded write/edit primitive whose compare-and-set semantics are not established as an existing DSH capability.
advisory_hypotheses.basis: Section 6.1 states the coordinator owns the first durable charge through one version-guarded execution.json update using the runtime's native guarded file write/edit operation and that a stale-version conflict aborts, but no pinned capability manifest is present in the reviewed bytes.
missing_project_sot: The pinned DSH tool/capability manifest and version that documents the guarded write operation's version-check and abort semantics.
advisory_hypotheses.suggested_validation: Inspect the pinned DSH capability manifest and exercise a stale-version write to prove abort/no-write, then bind the exact tool identity/hash in P15; otherwise record the capability as unproven.

advisory_hypotheses.claim: The pinned v32 consistency audit may contain the CS/CH/CA/BA findings and their closure evidence in an artifact supplied to another lane rather than to this one.
advisory_hypotheses.basis: The design references the v32 pre-council consistency audit but this lane's context omits internal-history and peer-findings, and no audit identifier appears in the reviewed bytes.
missing_project_sot: The pinned v32 pre-council consistency-audit bytes and any per-finding closure table maintained outside the design.
advisory_hypotheses.suggested_validation: Obtain the pinned audit and check each finding ID against a specific v33 locator; if any finding lacks a v33 locator, report it as an open closure item rather than accepting the Section 2 narrative.

advisory_hypotheses.claim: If implementers reuse the pre-reservation symbol G instead of the persisted running committed total, a reservation following a PostChargeRecoveryAllocation could be admitted on a stale ceiling and permit an overrun.
advisory_hypotheses.basis: Section 6.3 defines G as global committed units before a reservation while also persisting global_committed_units, and the recovery formula is written as global_committed_units := G+R+D; the text does not restate that a later reservation reads the persisted value as its G.
missing_project_sot: The authoritative AdministrativeResourceLedger schema/validator and its budget-arithmetic fixtures.
advisory_hypotheses.suggested_validation: Implement the stated formulas literally and run the described fixtures plus a second reservation after a recovery allocation, checking that global_remaining_units never goes negative and that debits reconcile.
